summary: Whole-roadmap target plan for enhanced derived categories of sheaves. It imports the 169 targets of the two accepted parts (E0–E4 and E5) unchanged and pinned by hash, corrects thirteen of them where this pass moves a dependency or a statement, and adds 32 targets: the cotangent complex of animated rings and its basic theory, moved down from DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.0 as animated refinements of the ordinary cotangent complex that DerivedModuleAlgebra (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) owns upstream; the ∞-category of spectra and the Eilenberg–Mac Lane module comparison, replacing citations of StableHomotopyKTheory; the geometric descendability and h-descent results of Bhatt–Scholze §11 for noetherian and perfect schemes; Hinich's symmetric monoidal structure on D∞(O); slice-free generators of module sheaves; the Amitsur tower and completion theorems of Carlsson; filtered objects; Kan extensions along arbitrary functors; perfect modules; the projection formula; completed base change; and the BMPSTWW warning about colimits in triangulated categories. Every paper item routed to this roadmap is accounted for, and every request other roadmaps address to it is triaged. All stages are planned; none is closed.

nodes.title: Enhanced sequential colimits versus colimits in the triangulated category
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M_0 → M_1 → M_2 → ⋯ a sequential diagram in the enhanced derived category D∞(R). Its colimit in D∞(R) exists, is the cofibre of 1 − (shift) on ⊕_i M_i (the mapping telescope), and commutes with cohomology: H^n(colim_i M_i) = colim_i H^n(M_i) for every n. In the homotopy category D(R), Mathlib's triangulated DerivedCategory, every epimorphism is split, so a categorical colimit M of the image diagram, if one exists, receives a split epimorphism ⊕_i M_i → M. For R = ℤ, M_i = ℤ/p^i in degree 0 and transition maps 1 ↦ p, the enhanced colimit is ℚ_p/ℤ_p in degree 0, while ⊕_i ℤ/p^i → ℚ_p/ℤ_p has no section; so ℚ_p/ℤ_p with its canonical cocone is not a colimit of this diagram in D(ℤ). Every filtered colimit used by this roadmap and its consumers is the enhanced one.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; D∞(R) is the enhancement of E1/enhanced-derived-category.
Colimits in D∞(R) are ∞-categorical colimits; colimits in D(R) are ordinary categorical colimits in the homotopy category.
proofSteps: Sequential colimits exist in D∞(R) by presentability (E1/derived-presentability) and are computed by the telescope cofibre of 1 − shift on the direct sum; termwise filtered colimits of complexes are exact, so H^n commutes with them.
For the example, the telescope of ℤ/p^i under multiplication by p has H^0 = colim_i ℤ/p^i = ℚ_p/ℤ_p and no other cohomology.

In a pretriangulated category a map f : X → Y is an epimorphism exactly when the second map of its distinguished triangle vanishes, and then the triangle splits (Mathlib Pretriangulated.Triangle.mor₂_eq_zero_iff_epi₁ and Pretriangulated.exists_iso_binaryBiproduct_of_distTriang), so f is split.

If M is a categorical colimit, Hom(M, −) → ∏_i Hom(M_i, −) is injective, so ⊕_i M_i → M is an epimorphism and hence split. A section ℚ_p/ℤ_p → ⊕_i ℤ/p^i would make Hom(ℚ_p, ℚ_p/ℤ_p) ≠ 0 inject into Hom(ℚ_p, ⊕_i ℤ/p^i), which is zero because ℚ_p is divisible and ⊕_i ℤ/p^i has no nonzero divisible subgroup.
acceptance: H^0 of the enhanced colimit of ℤ/p → ℤ/p² → ⋯ (maps 1 ↦ p) is ℚ_p/ℤ_p and all other cohomology vanishes.
The map ⊕_i ℤ/p^i → ℚ_p/ℤ_p has no section in D(ℤ), so ℚ_p/ℤ_p with its canonical cocone is not a colimit in the triangulated category.
For a constant diagram with identity transitions both the enhanced colimit and a colimit in D(R) are the constant value.

sources.match: The authors explain that their arguments use filtered colimits in the ∞-categorical sense; the footnote shows that a colimit in the triangulated category D(R) would force a split epimorphism from the direct sum, which fails for the ℤ/p^i system whose correct colimit is ℚ_p/ℤ_p.

nodes.title: Slice-free module sheaves
nodes.statement: Let (C, O) be a ringed site with C small. For an object U of C let O_U = j_{U!}(O|_U) be the extension by zero of the restriction of O to the slice site C/U; equivalently the sheafification of the presheaf of O-modules V ↦ ⊕_{φ : V → U} O(V). Then: (i) Hom_O(O_U, F) ≅ F(U), naturally in the O-module sheaf F and in U, the bijection sending a morphism to the image of the canonical section over U; (ii) O_U is a flat O-module; (iii) every sheaf of O-modules is a quotient of a direct sum of sheaves O_{U_i}, so {O_U : U ∈ C} is a separating family of Mod(O); (iv) j_{U!} is exact and left adjoint to restriction. If C has a final object X then O_X ≅ O.
hypotheses: C is small, so that the generating family is a set.
O is a sheaf of rings on C; flatness and tensor statements use a commutative O.
proofSteps: Define O_U as the sheafification (PresheafOfModules.sheafification) of Mathlib's free presheaf of modules on the representable presheaf of U, (PresheafOfModules.free R).obj (yoneda.obj U), one of the objects of the class PresheafOfModules.freeYoneda. The bijection PresheafOfModules.freeYonedaEquiv and the sheafification adjunction give (i).
Sections of the free presheaf over V are free O(V)-modules; flatness of presheaves is sectionwise and sheafification preserves flatness (Stacks Modules on Sites Lemmas 18.28.7–18.28.8).

For each section s ∈ F(U) take the map O_U → F corresponding to s; the sum over all pairs (U, s) is surjective (Stacks Lemma 18.28.8(3)). On presheaves the separating property is PresheafOfModules.freeYoneda.isSeparating, transported here through sheafification.
Exactness of j_{U!} is Stacks Lemma 18.19.3: it is right exact as a left adjoint and injective on presheaf sections, and sheafification is exact.
acceptance: If X is a final object, O_X ≅ O and Hom(O_X, F) = F(X) = Γ(F).
For the two-point discrete space with constant sheaf R and U one point, O_U has zero sections over the other point and is not isomorphic to any SheafOfModules.free.
Every module sheaf on the site receives a surjection from a direct sum of sheaves O_U.

sources.locator: Section 18.19 (tag 03DH), Lemma 18.19.2 (tag 03DI) and equation (18.19.2.1) (tag 0G1V), pp. 20–21; Lemma 18.19.3 (tag 03DJ), p. 21
sources.match: Stacks constructs extension by zero for the localization of a ringed site at an object, shows it is an exact left adjoint of restriction, and identifies maps out of j_{U!}O_U with sections over U.
j_{U!}O_U is flat, and every sheaf of O-modules is a quotient of a direct sum of such sheaves, hence of a flat sheaf.

uses.how: sums of the flat sheaves O_U begin the free-cover staircase that produces functorial K-flat replacements
the objects O_U[n] form a set of generators of D∞(O), the input of presentability
K-flat complexes built from sums of O_U compute the derived tensor product
every complex of module sheaves has a K-flat resolution by complexes of sums of O_U

nodes.title: Detecting zero by localization and derived reduction
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring, g ∈ R a non-zero-divisor and C ∈ D(R). If C ⊗_R R[1/g] = 0 and C ⊗^L_R R/g = 0, then C = 0. The residue-field form of this test fails without noetherian hypotheses: if V is a perfect valuation ring that is not a field, with fraction field K, maximal ideal m and residue field k, then the V-module K/m in degree 0 is nonzero, yet (K/m) ⊗_V K = 0 and (K/m) ⊗^L_V k = 0.
hypotheses: g is a non-zero-divisor, so R/g = cofib(g : R → R).
The reduction is the derived tensor C ⊗^L_R R/g, not the cokernel of g on a chosen representative.
proofSteps: Localization is exact, so C[1/g] = 0 says that every H^i(C) is g-power torsion.
Tensoring C with the triangle R →g R → R/g and using C ⊗^L R/g = 0 shows that g acts invertibly on every H^i(C).
A module that is g-power torsion and on which g is invertible is zero, so all H^i(C) vanish.

For the counterexample, K/m is torsion, so it dies after ⊗_V K. As V is perfect and not a field, m is flat and m² = m; hence Tor_0^V(K/m, k) = K/(mK + m) = 0 and Tor_1^V(K/m, k) = ker(m ⊗ K/m → K/m) = ker(K/m² → K/m) = 0.
acceptance: For R = ℤ, g = p and C = ℚ_p/ℤ_p, C[1/p] = 0 but C ⊗^L ℤ/p has H^{−1} = ℤ/p; the underived reduction (ℚ_p/ℤ_p)/p = 0 would wrongly suggest C = 0.
For a perfect valuation ring V that is not a field, K/m is a nonzero module passing both residue-field tests.
If g is a unit the hypothesis C[1/g] = 0 alone gives C = 0.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.6 with its proof and Remark 6.7, p. 23
sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove that a complex killed by inverting a non-zero-divisor g and by derived reduction modulo g vanishes, and remark that over a perfect valuation ring residue-field tests do not suffice, with K/m as the example. The last sentence of Remark 6.7, contrasting noetherian rings, omits its '= 0' (recorded as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E34); the noetherian residue-field criterion is not a target of this node.

nodes.title: The valuation decomposition triangle for quasicoherent cohomology
nodes.statement: Let V be a perfect valuation ring with valuation |·| : V → Γ ∪ {0} and let α : Γ → Γ' be a homomorphism of ordered abelian groups with kernel Γ_0. Put V' = V[S^{-1}] with S = {f ∈ V : α(|f|) = 1}, I = {f ∈ V : α(|f|) < 1}, V_0 = V/I and V_0' = Frac(V_0). Then V' is a valuation ring with value group the image of α, V_0 is a valuation ring with value group Γ_0, I is an ideal of both V and V' with V'/I = V_0', and 0 → V → V' ⊕ V_0 → V_0' → 0 is exact. Consequently, for every qcqs perfect V-scheme X and K ∈ Dqc(X), RΓ(X, K) → RΓ(X_{V'}, K) ⊕ RΓ(X_{V_0}, K) → RΓ(X_{V_0'}, K) is a distinguished triangle, where X_W = X ×_{Spec V} Spec W and K is pulled back.
hypotheses: V is a perfect valuation ring; all rings V', V_0, V_0' are then perfect.
X is a qcqs perfect scheme over V and K ∈ Dqc(X).
proofSteps: Describe V, V', I inside the fraction field via the valuation: V' consists of the elements whose value lies in Γ_0·Γ_{≤1}, and I of those whose value is smaller than Γ_0. Hence I = ker(V → V_0) = ker(V' → V_0') and the sequence is exact.
V' is a localization and V_0, V_0' are quotients by radical ideals of perfect rings, so all are perfect, and Spec W → Spec V is a map of perfect schemes for W ∈ {V', V_0, V_0'}.
Derived base change on perfect schemes (E1/perfect-scheme-base-change) gives RΓ(X_W, K) ≃ RΓ(X, K) ⊗^L_V W; tensoring the exact sequence with RΓ(X, K) yields the triangle.
acceptance: For α = id_Γ: V' = V, V_0 = V_0' = k and the sequence is 0 → V → V ⊕ k → k → 0.
For α : Γ → 0: V' = K, V_0 = V, V_0' = K and the sequence is 0 → V → K ⊕ V → K → 0.
For a rank-two perfect valuation ring and α the projection to its rank-one quotient, the triangle expresses RΓ over V through the two rank-one pieces, the reduction used in BS17 Lemma 6.4.

sources.match: For a perfect valuation ring and a map of value groups, Bhatt and Scholze build the localization V', the quotient V_0 and its fraction field, prove the four-term exact sequence and deduce the distinguished triangle of derived global sections for any perfect V-scheme and quasicoherent complex from derived base change (their Lemma 3.18).

nodes.title: The projection formula for ringed topoi
nodes.statement: Let f : (Sh(C), O_C) → (Sh(D), O_D) be a morphism of ringed topoi, E ∈ D∞(O_C) and K ∈ D∞(O_D). The map Rf_*E ⊗^L_{O_D} K → Rf_*(E ⊗^L_{O_C} Lf^*K) adjoint to Lf^*(Rf_*E ⊗^L K) ≃ Lf^*Rf_*E ⊗^L Lf^*K → E ⊗^L Lf^*K is natural in E and K. It is an equivalence when K is perfect, in particular when K is a finite locally free O_D-module in degree 0. It is compatible with the base change maps of a commutative square of ringed topoi. For K not perfect it need not be an equivalence.
hypotheses: Perfect means locally on D quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite free O_D-modules.
Lf^* is the derived pullback of E1/ringed-pullback-pushforward, with its monoidal comparison Lf^*(A ⊗^L B) ≃ Lf^*A ⊗^L Lf^*B.
proofSteps: Build the map by adjunction from the counit Lf^*Rf_* → id and the monoidality of Lf^*.
Being an equivalence is local on D, so for perfect K reduce to a strictly perfect complex, then by stupid truncations and summands to K = O_D[n], where the map is the identity.
Compatibility with base change: compare the two composites of projection-formula maps and base-change maps (Stacks Remark 21.50.2).
For the failure without perfection, take the non-quasi-compact map f : ⊔_{n ∈ ℕ} Spec k → Spec k, E = O and K = ⊕_{i ∈ ℕ} k: the source is ⊕_i ∏_n k and the target ∏_n ⊕_i k.
acceptance: For K = O_D the map is the identity of Rf_*E.
For K = O_D^r it is the evident identification (Rf_*E)^r ≃ Rf_*(E^r).
For f : ⊔_{n ∈ ℕ} Spec k → Spec k, E = O and K = ⊕_{i ∈ ℕ} k the map ⊕_i ∏_n k → ∏_n ⊕_i k is not surjective, so the perfection hypothesis cannot be dropped.

sources.match: Stacks constructs the projection map for any morphism of ringed topoi, proves it is an isomorphism when K is perfect by reduction to K = O[n], and records its compatibility with base change.

nodes.title: Kan extensions along arbitrary functors
nodes.statement: Let δ : C_0 → C_1 be a functor of small ∞-categories and D an ∞-category. A left Kan extension of f_0 : C_0 → D along δ is a functor f_1 : C_1 → D with α : f_0 → f_1 ∘ δ exhibiting f_1 as left adjoint-universal. (i) If D admits colimits indexed by the slices C_0 ×_{C_1} (C_1)_{/c}, a left Kan extension exists and is computed pointwise: f_1(c) = colim of f_0 over C_0 ×_{C_1} (C_1)_{/c}; when all these colimits exist, left Kan extension δ_! is a functor left adjoint to restriction δ^*. Dually, right Kan extensions δ_* are computed by limits over C_0 ×_{C_1} (C_1)_{c/} and are right adjoint to δ^*. (ii) For δ fully faithful the unit f_0 → δ^*δ_!f_0 and the counit δ^*δ_*f_0 → f_0 are equivalences; this recovers E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion and its dual. (iii) For a group-like E_1-space G (a group anima) and q : BG → *, δ = q gives homotopy orbits q_! = (−)_{hG} ⊣ q^* (trivial action) ⊣ q_* = (−)^{hG} on Fun(BG, D) for any ∞-category D with colimits and limits indexed by BG, for example D = D∞(R). (iv) Kan extensions compose: (δ' ∘ δ)_! ≃ δ'_! ∘ δ_!. For coCartesian fibrations p : C_0 → S and q : C_1 → S and δ over S carrying p-coCartesian edges to q-coCartesian edges, a left extension along δ is a left Kan extension exactly when its restriction to every fibre is a left Kan extension along δ_s : (C_0)_s → (C_1)_s; so left Kan extension along δ commutes with restriction to fibres.
hypotheses: C_0 and C_1 are small; D admits the indexed colimits (limits for right Kan extensions).
The pointwise formula is part of the statement, not an extra hypothesis.
proofSteps: Factor δ through the mapping cylinder M(δ) and reduce to the full-inclusion case of E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion together with the retraction of M(δ) onto C_1 (HTT Proposition 4.3.3.7).

The pointwise formula: by HTT Definition 4.3.3.2 a left Kan extension along δ is a left Kan extension along the full inclusion of C_0 into the cylinder M(δ), computed pointwise there (E3/left-kan-extension-along-a-full-inclusion); restrict along the cofinal map from C_0 ×_{C_1} (C_1)_{/c} to the slice of the cylinder (E3/cofinality-to-a-fibre). For fully faithful δ the unit is an equivalence (HTT Proposition 4.3.3.8).
Dualize by passing to opposite categories for right Kan extensions.
For q : BG → * the slice over the unique object is BG itself, so q_! and q_* are the colimit and limit over BG.
Composition from uniqueness of adjoints; the fibrewise criterion is HTT Proposition 4.3.3.10.
acceptance: For δ : C_0 → * the left Kan extension is the colimit of f_0 and the right Kan extension its limit.
For δ fully faithful the restriction of δ_!f_0 to C_0 is f_0.
For G = ℤ/2 acting trivially on ℤ ∈ D∞(ℤ), π_{−n} of ℤ^{hℤ/2} is H^n(ℤ/2; ℤ), which is nonzero for every even n ≥ 0, so q_* is not the naive invariants.

sources.locator: §4.3.3, Definition 4.3.3.2 and Propositions 4.3.3.5, 4.3.3.7, 4.3.3.8 and 4.3.3.10, printed pp. 285–291
sources.match: Lurie defines left Kan extensions along arbitrary maps through the mapping cylinder, reduces them to Kan extensions along full inclusions, proves that left Kan extension is left adjoint to restriction (4.3.3.7), that the unit is an equivalence at objects where δ is fully faithful (4.3.3.8), and that along a map of coCartesian fibrations preserving coCartesian edges Kan extensions are detected fibrewise (4.3.3.10).

nodes.title: Products of lim¹ classes vanish
nodes.statement: Let C be a stable ∞-category with a bifunctor ⊗ that is exact and preserves sequential colimits in each variable, A ∈ C an object with a map μ : A ⊗ A → A, and F_0 → F_1 → ⋯ a sequential diagram with colimit F, so that F^{⊗a} = colim_i F_i^{⊗a}. Then π_0 Map(F^{⊗a}, A) has the Milnor filtration 0 → lim¹_i π_1 Map(F_i^{⊗a}, A) → π_0 Map(F^{⊗a}, A) → lim_i π_0 Map(F_i^{⊗a}, A) → 0, and the product x·y = μ ∘ (x ⊗ y) ∈ π_0 Map(F^{⊗(a+b)}, A) of two classes x, y lying in the lim¹ parts is zero. In particular, if every composite F_i^{⊗m} → A of the canonical maps is nullhomotopic, then so is F^{⊗2m} → A.
hypotheses: ⊗ is exact and commutes with sequential colimits in each variable.
Only ℕ-indexed diagrams are treated here; general index categories are E2/multiplicative-derived-limit-filtration.
proofSteps: Mapping spaces turn the colimit into a limit, Map(F^{⊗a}, A) ≃ lim_i Map(F_i^{⊗a}, A); the product–difference fibre sequence of E2/coherent-towers-and-roos, applied to mapping spectra, gives the displayed extension through its long exact sequence of homotopy groups.
The pairing Map(F_i^{⊗a}, A) × Map(F_i^{⊗b}, A) → Map(F_i^{⊗(a+b)}, A) induced by μ is a map of towers along the diagonal of ℕ × ℕ, which is cofinal.

The tower filtration on π_0 of a sequential limit is multiplicative for pairings of towers, so two filtration-one classes multiply into filtration two, which is lim² of an ℕ-indexed tower and therefore zero.
If each F_i^{⊗m} → A is null, the class of F^{⊗m} → A has filtration one, and F^{⊗2m} → A is its square under μ (up to the symmetry of ⊗), hence null.
acceptance: For a constant diagram with identity transitions the lim¹ terms vanish and the statement reduces to the m-fold bound itself.
In D(ℤ), lim¹ of the tower ℤ ← ℤ ← ⋯ (maps multiplication by p) is ℤ_p/ℤ ≠ 0, so a single lim¹ class need not vanish; only products of two do.
The resulting bound for the colimit is 2m, not m.

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove the sequential case of their uniform-index lemma: the map F^{⊗m} → A lies in the lim¹ subgroup of π_0, and the multiplication pairing kills products of lim¹ classes because they land in lim², which vanishes for towers.

nodes.title: The multiplicative derived-limit filtration
nodes.statement: Let I be a small filtered category such that derived limits over I^op of diagrams of abelian groups vanish above degree d. Let C be a stable ∞-category with I^op-indexed limits, X : I^op → C a diagram and z ∈ C. The groups π_* Map(z, lim X) carry a natural decreasing filtration F^0 ⊇ F^1 ⊇ ⋯ with F^{d+1} = 0, natural in z and in X, such that F^0/F^1 embeds in lim_{I^op} π_* Map(z, X_i) and F^s/F^{s+1} is a subquotient of lim^s_{I^op} π_{*+s} Map(z, X_i) for 1 ≤ s ≤ d. It is the filtration of the Bousfield–Kan spectral sequence of the cosimplicial replacement of X. If ⊗ is a bifunctor on C, exact and limit-compatible in each variable as required, the induced pairings on mapping groups satisfy F^s · F^t ⊆ F^{s+t}. For I = ℕ, d = 1, F^1 is the lim¹ subgroup of the product–difference sequence of E2/coherent-towers-and-roos and multiplicativity is E2/lim1-products-vanish.
hypotheses: I is filtered and lim^s over I^op of abelian-group diagrams vanishes for s > d.
Multiplicativity is asserted for pairings of diagrams that are compatible with the cosimplicial replacement.
proofSteps: Compute lim X as the totalization of the cosimplicial replacement Π^•X (products over strings in I^op) and take the spectral sequence of its Tot tower (HA §1.2.2, dually for towers).
Identify its E_2 term with lim^s π_t by the standard comparison of the cosimplicial replacement with derived limits of abelian groups.
Vanishing of lim^s for s > d makes the E_2 page live in columns 0 ≤ s ≤ d, so the spectral sequence degenerates at a finite stage and converges strongly; F^{d+1} = 0.

Multiplicativity: an Alexander–Whitney diagonal on the cosimplicial replacement gives a pairing of Tot towers raising filtration additively. The paper leaves the general case to the reader; its written proof is gap G-EDS-W1.
acceptance: For I with a final object, lim over I^op is evaluation at that object, so F^1 = 0.
For I = ℕ and the tower ℤ ← ℤ ← ⋯ (multiplication by p) in D(ℤ), with z = ℤ, the class group in degree −1 is F^1 = lim¹ = ℤ_p/ℤ and F^0/F^1 = 0.
For I = ℕ and a tower of surjections of abelian groups, F^1 = 0.

sources.locator: Lemma 11.22, statement for a filtered I whose inverse limits have finite cohomological dimension, p. 44
sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze state the uniform-index lemma for such I but write out only the sequential case, leaving the general case to the reader; this filtration is the input that case needs.
The spectral sequence of a filtered object of a stable ∞-category with a t-structure, and its convergence for exhaustive filtrations, used dually for the Tot tower.

uses.how: for a general index category, d + 1 classes of filtration one multiply to zero, bounding the descendability index of the colimit
the case I = ℕ, d = 1

nodes.title: Inductive level of proper surjections
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper surjective map of finite presentation between qcqs schemes. f has inductive level 0 if, after refinement, it factors as a proper fppf cover followed by a finitely presented nil-immersion onto Y. Inductively, f has inductive level ≤ n if, after refinement, it factors as X' → X_0 → Y_0 → Y where Y_0 → Y is a finitely presented nil-immersion, X' → X_0 is a proper fppf cover, and X_0 → Y_0 is proper, surjective, of finite presentation and an isomorphism outside a finitely presented closed subset Z ⊆ Y_0 such that X_0 ×_{Y_0} Z → Z has inductive level ≤ n − 1. A refinement of f is a proper surjection X'' → Y of finite presentation factoring through f. These notions are stable under base change, and every such f has finite inductive level.
hypotheses: Schemes are qcqs and all maps are of finite presentation.
Refinement is allowed at every step; level is an upper bound, not an invariant.
proofSteps: Stability under base change: each piece of the factorization (fppf cover, nil-immersion, isomorphism away from Z) is preserved by base change.

Finiteness: by absolute noetherian approximation (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0/noetherian-approximation) assume Y noetherian of dimension d; by generic flatness and flattening by blowup (SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4/flattening-by-blowup) refine f to a proper fppf cover of a blowup that is an isomorphism outside a closed Z with dim Z < dim Y, and induct on dimension. The proof in the source names the factorization through Z with a misprint recorded as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E3; the corrected induction is used here.
acceptance: A proper fppf cover has level 0.
A blowup of A² at the origin, an isomorphism outside a point, has level ≤ 1.
Level ≤ n is stable under base change along any map of qcqs schemes.

sources.locator: Definition 2.5 with the sentence after it, and Lemma 2.6, p. 5
sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze define the inductive level of a finitely presented proper surjection by factorizations through nil-immersions, proper fppf covers and modifications, note stability under base change, and prove finiteness by noetherian approximation and flattening by blowup.

nodes.title: Abstract blowup squares for h-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let S be a qcqs scheme and F an h-sheaf of spaces on the category of finitely presented S-schemes (h-topology generated by fppf covers and finitely presented proper surjections). Let Y be affine of finite presentation over S and X → Y a finitely presented proper surjection that is an isomorphism outside a finitely presented closed Z ⊆ Y with preimage E. Then F(Y) → F(X) ×_{F(E)} F(Z) is an equivalence. In particular F(Y) ≃ F(X) for a finitely presented nil-immersion X → Y (take Z = X).
hypotheses: F is a sheaf of spaces (an ∞-sheaf) for the h-topology, not only a presheaf of sets.
The square is a pullback in spaces; F(E) is the value on the reduced preimage of Z or any finitely presented scheme structure on it.
proofSteps: Let h_T denote the h-sheafification of the representable presheaf of T. For sheaves of sets, X ⊔ (E ×_Z E) → X ×_Y X is an h-cover, so h_Y is the pushout h_X ⊔_{h_E} h_Z in h-sheaves of sets (BS17 Proposition 2.8).

h_E → h_X is a monomorphism sectionwise, so the set-theoretic pushout of presheaves is a homotopy pushout of presheaves of spaces; sheafification preserves pushouts and the result is discrete, hence equal to h_Y as an ∞-sheaf.
Mapping into F turns the pushout into the claimed pullback.
acceptance: For Z = ∅ the statement is F(Y) ≃ F(X) for a finitely presented proper surjection that is an isomorphism, which is trivial.
For a nil-immersion X → Y and Z = X, F(Y) ≃ F(X): h-sheaves do not see nilpotents.
For the blowup X → A² at the origin, F(A²) ≃ F(X) ×_{F(P¹)} F(point).

sources.locator: Proposition 2.8 and its proof, p. 6; Theorem 2.9, first half of the proof, p. 7
sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze show that abstract blowup squares give pullbacks for h-sheaves of sets and then of spaces, by exhibiting the representable h-sheaf of Y as the pushout of those of X and Z along E, following Voevodsky.

nodes.title: Descendable algebra maps from algebraic geometry
nodes.statement: Fix a map f : X → Y of qcqs schemes and work in the presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories Dqc(−). (1) For a finite cover of X by quasi-compact opens j_i : U_i → X, O_X → ∏_i Rj_{i,*}O_{U_i} is descendable. (2) If f is fppf, O_Y → Rf_*O_X is descendable. (3) If I ⊆ O_X is a nilpotent quasicoherent ideal, O_X → O_X/I is descendable. (4) If A → B is descendable in CAlg(Dqc(X)), then Rf_*A → Rf_*B is descendable in Dqc(Y). In the affine case (2) is: a faithfully flat finitely presented map of rings is descendable.
hypotheses: Descendable is in the sense of E5:abstract/descendable-algebras.
In (2), finite presentation of f is used through the countable-presentation criterion; f is fppf, so locally of finite presentation.
proofSteps: (1): Dqc(X) is the finite limit of the categories Dqc(U_{i_1} ∩ ⋯ ∩ U_{i_k}); descendability is detected on the vertices of a finite limit (E5:abstract/module-descent-and-functoriality), and on U_i the map has a retraction, so it is descendable by passage to an intermediate algebra.

(2): by (1) and preservation under colimit-preserving lax monoidal functors reduce to affine X and Y; a faithfully flat map whose target is countably presented is descendable (Mathew16 Corollary 3.33).
(3): the finite filtration 0 = I^k ⊆ ⋯ ⊆ I ⊆ O_X has graded pieces that are O_X/I-modules, so O_X lies in the thick tensor ideal generated by O_X/I (Mathew16 Proposition 3.35).
(4): Rf_* is colimit-preserving and lax symmetric monoidal on Dqc of qcqs schemes, so it preserves a finite descendability index.
acceptance: For the cover of Spec ℤ[a, b, c, d]/(ab + cd − 1) by the two basic opens a ≠ 0 and c ≠ 0, the map to the product is descendable, of index at most 5 (BS17 Example 11.19).
R → R/I with I nilpotent of order k has index at most k.
ℤ → ℤ/p is not descendable although Spec ℤ/p → Spec ℤ is a closed immersion: (3) needs a nilpotent ideal.

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze list four sources of descendable maps in quasicoherent derived categories: finite quasi-compact open covers, fppf maps, nilpotent thickenings and pushforward. Their citation of Mathew for (2) has a misprint recorded as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E22.

Mathew proves descendability is detected on a finite limit of stable homotopy theories, that faithfully flat maps with countably presented target are descendable, and that quotients by nilpotent ideals are descendable.

nodes.title: Descendability of h-covers of noetherian schemes
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be an h-cover of noetherian schemes (a map that is a cover for the h-topology generated by fppf covers and finitely presented proper surjections). Then O_Y → Rf_*O_X is descendable in Dqc(Y).
hypotheses: X and Y are noetherian.
Descendable is in the sense of E5:abstract/descendable-algebras, in CAlg(Dqc(Y)).
proofSteps: Descendability may be checked after replacing f by a refinement (passage to an intermediate algebra) and locally on Y (E2/descendable-maps-from-geometry (1), (4)); so assume Y = Spec A affine and f proper surjective, of inductive level ≤ n (E2/proper-surjection-inductive-level).
Induct on n. For n = 0, f is after refinement an fppf cover followed by a nil-immersion; combine (2), (3) and (4) of E2/descendable-maps-from-geometry with composition of descendable maps.

For n > 0 reduce to f an isomorphism outside Z = V(I). The fibre F of O_Y → Rf_*O_X has bounded coherent cohomology (coherence of proper pushforward, AdicSpacesPartII:F0/graded-cohomology-finiteness) supported on Z (flat base change to Y − Z, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2/tor-independent-base-change), so it is an O_Y/I^N-complex for N ≫ 0; replace I by I^N.

By induction O_Z → R(f_Z)_*O_{f^{-1}Z} is descendable, so for some k the map F^{⊗k} → O_Y → O_Z is null and F^{⊗k} → O_Y factors through I; then F^{⊗(k+1)} → O_Y factors through the multiplication I ⊗ F → F, which is null since F is an O_Y/I-complex.
The source names this N with the same letter as the inductive level and cites 'Proposition 2.6' for Lemma 2.6 (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E48, E49); the corrected argument is used.
acceptance: A finite surjective map of noetherian schemes, for example the normalization of a nodal curve, gives a descendable structure map.
The blowup of A²_k at the origin gives a descendable O_{A²} → Rf_*O_X.
Spec(k) ⊔ Spec(k[x, 1/x]) → Spec(k[x]) is surjective but not an h-cover and is not descendable (E2/descendability-detects-noetherian-h-covers).

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove, adapting an argument of Mathew for finite maps, that h-covers of noetherian schemes give descendable maps on derived pushforwards of structure sheaves, by induction on the inductive level and a nilpotence argument for the fibre supported on the bad locus.

nodes.title: h-descent for quasicoherent complexes on noetherian schemes
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be an h-cover of noetherian schemes with S affine, and B = Rf_*O_X ∈ CAlg(Dqc(S)). Then Dqc(S) ≃ lim_{[n] ∈ Δ} Mod_{B^{⊗(n+1)}}(Dqc(S)), the limit along extension of scalars, and O_S ≃ lim_Δ B^{⊗(•+1)}. If X = Spec C is affine, B^{⊗(n+1)} is the derived tensor power C^{⊗L(n+1)} over A = Γ(S, O_S), viewed in CAlg(D(A)). Identifying Mod_{B^{⊗(n+1)}}(Dqc(S)) with Dqc of the derived (n+1)-fold fibre product of X over S gives the derived Čech-nerve form of the statement; that identification needs derived schemes and is not part of this node. The statement does not extend to derived bases: for A = Sym_ℂ(ℂ[2]) the map A → π_0A is an h-cover of derived schemes, but extension of scalars D(A) → D(π_0A) is not conservative.
hypotheses: X and S are noetherian; S affine in the module form.
Tensor products are derived throughout.
proofSteps: By E2/noetherian-h-cover-descendability, O_S → B is descendable.
Apply module descent for descendable algebras (E5:abstract/module-descent-and-functoriality, BS17 Theorem 11.15).
For affine X = Spec C, B^{⊗(n+1)} is computed by derived tensor powers of C over A (E1/presentability-and-derived-tensor).
For the derived counterexample, π_*(A) = ℂ[u] with |u| = 2; K = A[u^{-1}] is nonzero while K ⊗_A π_0A = 0, so base change to π_0A is not conservative and descent fails.
acceptance: For a Zariski cover the statement is Zariski descent for Dqc.
For a finite surjective map of noetherian rings A → C, D(A) is the limit of the module categories of the derived tensor powers of C.
For A = Sym_ℂ(ℂ[2]) the complex A[u^{-1}] is nonzero and killed by base change to π_0A, so no descent holds for this cover of derived schemes.

sources.locator: Theorem 11.12 and its proof, p. 42 and p. 45; Remark 11.13, p. 42
sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove that quasicoherent complexes on noetherian schemes satisfy descent along the derived Čech nerve of an h-cover, using descendability and Mathew's module descent; they remark that the result fails for derived schemes, with the free algebra on a degree-two class as the example. The statement misnames the Čech nerve (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E14), and footnote 22 on detecting pseudo-coherence is incomplete (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E47); this node uses neither.

nodes.title: Descendability characterizes h-covers of noetherian rings
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a finitely presented map of noetherian rings. Then Spec B → Spec A is an h-cover if and only if A → B is descendable in CAlg(D(A)).
hypotheses: A and B are discrete noetherian rings and B is finitely presented over A.
proofSteps: If: by E2/noetherian-h-cover-descendability.

Only if: descendability is stable under base change, so it suffices to show that Spec B → Spec A is a topological quotient, because finitely presented maps of noetherian schemes that are universal topological quotients are h-covers (gap G-EDS-W3).

Quasi-compact opens of Spec A correspond to idempotent algebras C ∈ CAlg(D(A)) with C ⊗_A C ≃ C, compact as commutative algebras and bounded above (gap G-EDS-W2). Descent gives CAlg(D(A)) ≃ lim CAlg(D(B^{⊗L(•+1)})) and, with descent of compactness, an equivalence of these posets of opens.

If V ⊆ Spec A has quasi-compact open preimage U, the two pullbacks of U to Spec(B ⊗^L_A B) agree, so U descends to a quasi-compact open W of Spec A with preimage U; surjectivity of Spec B → Spec A forces W = V.
acceptance: A Zariski cover A → ∏ A[1/f_i] with (f_i) = A is descendable and an h-cover.
k[x] → k × k[x, 1/x] is surjective on spectra but not a topological quotient, and it is not descendable.
ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is finitely presented, but Spec 𝔽_p → Spec ℤ_p misses the generic point, so it is not an h-cover; correspondingly it is not descendable (BS17 Remark 11.16).

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove that a finitely presented map of noetherian rings is descendable exactly when it is an h-cover, using Proposition 11.25 for one direction and, for the other, Bhatt–Halpern-Leistner's description of quasi-compact opens by idempotent algebras together with Voevodsky's characterization of h-covers of noetherian schemes as universal topological quotients.

For a spectral algebraic stack, pushforward of structure sheaves identifies quasi-compact open substacks with commutative algebras that are localizations of the unit, compact as algebras and bounded above.

nodes.title: Derived patching along abstract blowups of perfect schemes
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper surjective finitely presented map of qcqs 𝔽_p-schemes that is an isomorphism over a quasi-compact open U ⊆ Y; let Z = Y ∖ U and E = f^{-1}(Z) (with finitely presented scheme structures). Then pullback induces an equivalence of ∞-categories Dqc(Y_perf) ≃ Dqc(X_perf) ×_{Dqc(E_perf)} Dqc(Z_perf), and likewise for perfect complexes Perf(−_perf), which are the dualizable objects.
hypotheses: Schemes are qcqs over 𝔽_p and f is finitely presented, proper and surjective.
The fibre product is the pullback of ∞-categories.
proofSteps: The presheaf T ↦ Dqc(T_perf) on finitely presented 𝔽_p-schemes is an h-sheaf of ∞-categories by E2/perfect-h-cech-descent (perfection sends h-covers to h-covers in Perf and fibre products to fibre products).
Apply E2/abstract-blowup-squares to its underlying sheaf of spaces, and to mapping spaces, to obtain the equivalence of ∞-categories.
Pass to dualizable objects: the equivalence is symmetric monoidal, so it restricts to Perf.
acceptance: For U = Y (Z = ∅) both sides are Dqc(Y_perf).
For the blowup of A² at the origin, a perfect complex on the perfected plane is the same as one on the perfected blowup with a compatible one on the perfected point.

Without perfection the statement fails for Dqc of ordinary schemes: for the nil-immersion X = Spec k → Y = Spec k[ε]/(ε²), with U = ∅ and Z = E = Spec k (reduced structure), the right side is D(k) but Dqc(Y) = D(k[ε]/(ε²)) is not D(k).

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze deduce from h-descent on perfect schemes and their h-sheaf criterion that quasicoherent complexes on the perfection of the base glue from those on the perfections of an abstract blowup square, and likewise for perfect complexes.

nodes.title: Truncated maps to hypercomplete objects
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳 be an ∞-topos, G a hypercomplete object and F → G an n-truncated morphism for some n < ∞. Then F is hypercomplete.
hypotheses: n is finite.
proofSteps: Hypercompleteness of F means locality with respect to ∞-connective maps T → T'.

In the slice 𝒳/G, F is an n-truncated object, hence hypercomplete there (HTT Lemma 6.5.2.9), and a map of 𝒳/G is ∞-connective exactly when its image in 𝒳 is (HTT Proposition 6.5.1.19; the source cites 6.5.1.18, recorded as PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17/E51).
Combine with hypercompleteness of G to lift maps from T to F along ∞-connective T → T'.
acceptance: If G is final (hence hypercomplete in a hypercomplete topos), every truncated object is hypercomplete.
A (−1)-truncated map (a monomorphism) into a hypercomplete object has hypercomplete source; this is how BS17 deduces hypercompleteness of Dqc from that of the sheaf of module categories.
The finiteness of n cannot be dropped: an ∞-connective map T → G with T not equivalent to G is not truncated.

sources.match: Bhatt and Scholze prove that an n-truncated map into a hypercomplete object of an ∞-topos has hypercomplete source, using that truncated objects are hypercomplete and that connectivity is detected in slices.

sources.locator: Lemma 6.5.2.9, printed p. 669; Proposition 6.5.1.19, printed p. 664
sources.match: Truncated objects of an ∞-topos are hypercomplete; a morphism in a slice topos is n-connective exactly when its image is.

nodes.title: Amitsur completion of finitely generated modules
nodes.statement: Let A be a noetherian ring, I ⊆ A an ideal, B = A/I and M a finitely generated A-module. The totalization of the Amitsur cosimplicial object M ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)} in D(A) is the I-adic completion: Tot(M ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)}) ≃ M^∧_I = lim_n M/I^n M, concentrated in degree 0, compatibly with the maps from M. In particular the Amitsur totalization of ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is ℤ_p, although ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is not descendable.
hypotheses: A is noetherian and M is finitely generated; both are used, through the Artin–Rees lemma.
Tensor products are derived; Tot is the limit in D∞(A).
proofSteps: For a B-module N (so IN = 0) the augmented Amitsur object N ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)} has an extra degeneracy, so Tot(N ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)}) ≃ N; Tot is exact, so by the finite filtration by the B-modules I^jM/I^{j+1}M, Tot(M/I^kM ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)}) ≃ M/I^kM for every k.

Carlsson's comparison (proof of Theorem 4.4): in each cosimplicial degree s, the pro-system {MultiTor^A_*(B, …, B, M/I^kM)}_k (s + 1 factors B) is pro-isomorphic to the constant system with value MultiTor^A_*(B, …, B, M), because I-adic pro-systems are exact on finitely generated modules over a noetherian ring (Artin–Rees) and I acts trivially on these multi-Tor groups, so the I-adic pro-system of the multi-Tor of M is pro-zero. Totalization commutes with inverse limits, so Tot(M ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)}) ≃ R lim_k Tot(M/I^kM ⊗^L_A B^{⊗L(•+1)}) (E2/pro-towers, E2/pro-zero-derived-limit).

Hence the totalization is R lim_k M/I^kM; the tower is surjective, so lim¹ vanishes (E2/tower-milnor) and the result is M^∧_I in degree 0, compared with the classical completion by E4/classical-completion-comparison.
For A = ℤ_p, I = (p) and M = A this gives ℤ_p, while ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is not descendable since it becomes the zero ring map after inverting p (E5:abstract/descendable-algebras).
acceptance: For A = ℤ, I = (p), M = ℤ the totalization is ℤ_p, not ℤ: the Amitsur totalization completes.
If I is nilpotent the tower {M/I^n M} is eventually constant and the totalization is M.
For A = ℤ_p and I = (p) the totalization of the Čech nerve of ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is ℤ_p, so recovering the unit by totalization is strictly weaker than descendability.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.4 and its proof, p. 11; Example 8.1, p. 30
sources.match: Carlsson proves that for a noetherian ring and a finitely generated module the derived completion along A → A/I, the totalization of the Amitsur complex, is the I-adic completion, by comparing the pro-systems of multi-Tor groups of M/I^kM with those of M; he notes the example of ℤ → 𝔽_p.
Bhatt and Scholze observe that ℤ_p → 𝔽_p is not descendable although its Čech nerve totalizes to ℤ_p, citing Carlsson's theorem.

nodes.title: Completed extension of scalars
nodes.statement: Let φ : R → S be a map of commutative rings, I ⊆ R and J ⊆ S finitely generated ideals with φ(I)S ⊆ √J. For K ∈ D(R) put K ⊗̂^L_R S := (K ⊗^L_R S)^∧_J, the derived J-completion (E4/the-imported-completion-interface on the point topos). Restriction of scalars sends Dcomp(S, J) into Dcomp(R, I), and K ↦ K ⊗̂^L_R S, restricted to Dcomp(R, I), is left adjoint to it: Hom_{Dcomp(S,J)}(K ⊗̂^L_R S, L) ≃ Hom_{D(R)}(K, L). It is symmetric monoidal for the completed tensor products, transitive along (R, I) → (S, J) → (T, L) and unital for the identity, and compatible with reduction: (K ⊗̂^L_R S) ⊗^L_S S/J ≃ K ⊗^L_R S/J. If R → S is flat, J = IS and R/I → S/IS is an isomorphism, restriction Dcomp(S, IS) → Dcomp(R, I) is an equivalence with inverse K ↦ K ⊗̂^L_R S. Commutative algebra objects go to commutative algebra objects. If S is derived J-complete and K is perfect, K ⊗̂^L_R S ≃ K ⊗^L_R S. On the point topos the derived completion used here is the module completion that DerivedModuleAlgebra §§1.2–1.5 (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) constructs.
hypotheses: I and J are finitely generated, so derived completion is a left adjoint and is computed by the Koszul or Čech formula.
φ(I)S ⊆ √J is needed for restriction to land in I-complete objects.
proofSteps: Derived completeness for J implies completeness for every ideal inside √J, because the set of f ∈ S with T(L, f) = 0 is a radical ideal (Stacks Lemma 15.93.2); so L ∈ Dcomp(S, J) is IS-complete and its restriction is I-complete (Stacks Lemma 15.93.24).
Adjunction: Hom(K ⊗̂ S, L) = Hom_{D(S)}(K ⊗^L S, L) = Hom_{D(R)}(K, L) by the completion adjunction and extension of scalars.

Transitivity and units follow from uniqueness of left adjoints; monoidality from the fact that completion inverts maps that are equivalences after ⊗^L S/J, and the completed tensor product is the completion of the tensor product (E4/completed-sheaf-tensor).
Reduction: completion does not change K ⊗^L S/J. The flat case is Stacks Lemma 15.93.25.
Perfect K: K ⊗^L_R S is a finite colimit of shifts of retracts of S, and derived complete objects are closed under finite colimits, shifts and retracts.
acceptance: Identity: for (R, I) → (R, I) and complete K, K ⊗̂ R ≃ K.
For (ℤ, (p)) → (ℤ_p, (p)) and K = ℤ the result is ℤ_p; for K = ℚ it is 0.
For R = ℤ_p, S = ℤ_p[x] and J = (p), ℤ_p ⊗̂ S is the p-adically completed polynomial ring, not ℤ_p[x], which is not p-complete.

sources.match: Stacks shows that the elements for which an object is derived complete form a radical ideal, that derived completion is left adjoint to the inclusion of complete objects for finitely generated ideals, that restriction along a ring map preserves completeness for the extended ideal, and that it is an equivalence for flat maps inducing an isomorphism modulo the ideal.

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal derived category of module sheaves
nodes.statement: Let (C, O) be a small ringed site with O commutative. D∞(O) carries a symmetric monoidal ∞-category structure whose tensor bifunctor is the derived tensor product of E1/presentability-and-derived-tensor and whose unit is O[0]. It is the symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localization of the symmetric monoidal category of K-flat complexes of O-modules (total tensor product of TauCeti.SheafOfModules.tensorProduct termwise) at the quasi-isomorphisms. The tensor product preserves colimits separately in each variable, so D∞(O) is presentably symmetric monoidal and stable, a stable homotopy theory in the sense used for descendability. For a morphism of ringed topoi f, Lf^* is symmetric monoidal and its right adjoint Rf_* is lax symmetric monoidal; in particular RΓ(C, −) : D∞(O) → D∞(Γ(C, O)) is lax symmetric monoidal and gives natural cup products RΓ(K) ⊗^L RΓ(M) → RΓ(K ⊗^L M), associative, unital and graded commutative; for a ring map A → Γ(C, O), composing with restriction of scalars gives the cup product RΓ(K) ⊗^L_A RΓ(M) → RΓ(K ⊗^L M) in D(A), and on cohomology classes x of degree i and y of degree j, x ∪ y = (−1)^{ij} y ∪ x under the symmetry of K ⊗^L M. No hypothesis on points of the topos is used.
hypotheses: C small; O a sheaf of commutative rings.
The localization is the ∞-categorical one; on homotopy categories it gives the derived tensor of Mathlib's DerivedCategory when C is a point.
proofSteps: K-flat complexes are closed under total tensor products (Stacks Lemma 21.17.5) and contain O; tensoring with a K-flat complex preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes (Stacks Lemma 21.17.12).

So the symmetric monoidal category of K-flat complexes and the class of quasi-isomorphisms satisfy the hypothesis of Hinich's theorem; E5:abstract/monoidal-dwyer-kan-localization (NS18 Proposition A.5) gives a symmetric monoidal localization whose underlying category is the Dwyer–Kan localization.
Functorial K-flat replacement (E1/k-flat-replacement) identifies that underlying localization with D∞(O), compatibly with the derived tensor bifunctor of E1.

Colimit preservation is the E1 statement; pullback of K-flat complexes is K-flat and termwise symmetric monoidal, so Lf^* is symmetric monoidal by the universal property of the localization; its right adjoint is lax symmetric monoidal (HA Corollary 7.3.2.7). Cup products are the lax structure maps of RΓ.
acceptance: On the point site with O = ℤ, ℤ/p ⊗ ℤ/p has H^{−1} = H^0 = ℤ/p.
O[0] is a unit: O ⊗ K ≃ K naturally.
The construction never assumes enough points: it applies to the pro-étale and v-sites.

sources.locator: Definition A.4 and Proposition A.5, pp. 129–130
sources.match: Nikolaus and Scholze define the symmetric monoidal Dwyer–Kan localization and state Hinich's theorem: if the tensor product preserves weak equivalences in each variable, the localization is symmetric monoidal, the localization functor is symmetric monoidal, and lax and strong monoidal functors out of it are those inverting the weak equivalences.
Total tensor products of K-flat complexes of modules on a ringed site are K-flat, and tensoring with a quasi-isomorphism of K-flat complexes gives a quasi-isomorphism.
A right adjoint of a symmetric monoidal functor between symmetric monoidal ∞-categories is a map of ∞-operads, that is, lax symmetric monoidal.

nodes.title: Fibres of the Amitsur tower
nodes.statement: Let C be a presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category, A → B a map in CAlg(C), F = fib(A → B) ∈ Mod_A(C) and M ∈ Mod_A(C). For the partial totalizations Tot_k of the Amitsur cosimplicial A-module M ⊗_A B^{⊗_A(•+1)}, there are natural fibre sequences F^{⊗_A(k+1)} ⊗_A M → M → Tot_k(M ⊗_A B^{⊗_A(•+1)}), compatible in k, in which the map F^{⊗(k+2)} → F^{⊗(k+1)} is induced by F → A on one factor. Hence the fibre of the map of towers {M} → {Tot_k} is the tower {F^{⊗(k+1)} ⊗_A M}, and the augmented Amitsur tower is pro-constant exactly when this fibre tower is pro-zero.
hypotheses: Tensor products are relative to A and exact in each variable.
proofSteps: Induct on k. For k = 0, Tot_0 = M ⊗_A B and the fibre of M → M ⊗_A B is F ⊗_A M.
The fibre of Tot_k → Tot_{k−1} is the k-fold desuspension of the k-th normalized term, M ⊗_A B ⊗_A (cofib(A → B))^{⊗k} ≃ Σ^k(M ⊗_A B ⊗_A F^{⊗k}).

Tensoring F → A → B with F^{⊗k} ⊗ M gives the cofibre sequence F^{⊗(k+1)} ⊗ M → F^{⊗k} ⊗ M → F^{⊗k} ⊗ B ⊗ M; comparing with the previous step gives the sequence for k and its compatibility with k − 1.
acceptance: For A = B, F = 0 and every Tot_k is M.
For ℤ → ℤ/p in D(ℤ), F = ℤ mapping by p, F^{⊗(k+1)} → ℤ is multiplication by p^{k+1}, and Tot_k of the Amitsur complex of ℤ is ℤ/p^{k+1}: the tower is the p-adic tower.
For k = 0 the statement is the fibre sequence F ⊗ M → M → M ⊗ B.

nodes.title: Spectra and stabilization
nodes.statement: For an ∞-category C with finite limits, the ∞-category Sp(C) of spectrum objects is the category of reduced excisive functors from pointed finite spaces to C; for C pointed it is the limit of the tower ⋯ → C →Ω C →Ω C, with Ω^∞ : Sp(C) → C the projection to the last term. Sp(C) is stable, and Ω^∞ is an equivalence exactly when C is stable. The ∞-category of spectra is Sp = Sp(S_*), with sphere spectrum 𝕊 = Σ^∞_+(*). For any stable C and X ∈ C, the left exact functor Map_C(X, −) lifts uniquely to an exact functor map_C(X, −) : C → Sp, the mapping spectrum, with Ω^∞ map_C(X, Y) ≃ Map_C(X, Y) and π_n map_C(X, Y) = π_0 Map_C(X, Σ^{−n}Y) for every integer n. For presentable C, Ω^∞ has a left adjoint Σ^∞; Sp is presentable, stable and compactly generated by 𝕊, and the presentable stable ∞-categories are exactly the Sp-modules in PrL, Sp being an idempotent algebra there.
hypotheses: C has finite limits; stability and presentability are hypotheses where stated.
proofSteps: Define Sp(C) as reduced excisive functors and identify it with the tower limit (HA Definition 1.4.2.8 and Proposition 1.4.2.24).
Stability of Sp(C) and the criterion for Ω^∞ to be an equivalence: HA Corollary 1.4.2.17 and Proposition 1.4.2.21.
Mapping spectra: a left exact functor out of a stable category factors uniquely through Ω^∞ (HA Corollary 1.4.2.23).
For presentable C, Ω^∞ preserves limits and is accessible, so it has a left adjoint (E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations); compact generation of Sp is HA Proposition 1.4.3.7 for C = S_*.
Sp is an idempotent algebra in PrL and its modules are the presentable stable categories (HA Proposition 4.8.2.18).
acceptance: Sp is stable and Ω^∞ : Sp → S_* is not an equivalence.
For a stable C, Ω^∞ : Sp(C) → C is an equivalence.
In D(ℤ), π_{−n} map(ℤ, ℤ/p) = Hom_{D(ℤ)}(ℤ, ℤ/p[n]), which is ℤ/p for n = 0 and zero otherwise.

sources.locator: Definition 1.4.2.8, p. 142; Corollary 1.4.2.17 and Proposition 1.4.2.21, p. 146; Corollary 1.4.2.23 and Proposition 1.4.2.24, p. 147; Definition 1.4.3.1, p. 150; Propositions 1.4.3.6–1.4.3.7, pp. 151–152; Proposition 4.8.2.18, p. 722
sources.match: Lurie defines spectrum objects as reduced excisive functors, proves they form a stable ∞-category equal to the Ω-tower limit, characterizes stable categories by Ω^∞ being an equivalence, lifts left exact functors from stable categories to spectra, defines Sp and shows that it is compactly generated and that Sp-modules in PrL are the presentable stable categories.

nodes.title: Filtered objects and the filtered derived category
nodes.statement: Let C be a presentable stable ∞-category and ℤ^op the poset of integers with a map n → m exactly when n ≥ m. The filtered category is DF(C) = Fun(ℤ^op, C); for F ∈ DF(C) put F(−∞) = colim_i F(i) (the underlying object), F(∞) = lim_i F(i) and gr^i F = cofib(F(i+1) → F(i)). F is complete if F(∞) = 0; complete objects form a full subcategory D̂F(C) whose inclusion has a left adjoint F ↦ F̂ with F̂(i) = cofib(F(∞) → F(i)), commuting with every gr^i. The functors gr^i together with F ↦ F(∞) are jointly conservative on DF(C), and the gr^i alone on D̂F(C). DF(C) and D̂F(C) have all limits and colimits; evaluation and gr^i preserve them on DF(C), and gr^i preserves those of D̂F(C). If C is presentably symmetric monoidal, Day convolution makes DF(C) presentably symmetric monoidal with (F ⊗ G)(i) = colim_{j+k ≥ i} F(j) ⊗ G(k) and gr^n(F ⊗ G) ≃ ⊕_{i+j=n} gr^i F ⊗ gr^j G; D̂F(C) has a unique symmetric monoidal structure for which completion is symmetric monoidal. For C = D∞(R) this is the filtered derived category DF(R), and for C = D∞(O) the filtered derived category of module sheaves on a ringed site.
hypotheses: C presentable stable; for the monoidal part, presentably symmetric monoidal.
Filtrations are decreasing and indexed by all integers; no exhaustiveness is imposed.
proofSteps: Functor categories into presentable stable categories are presentable stable, with limits and colimits computed pointwise (E0/coherent-functors, E5:presentability/presentable-categories).
Completion is the cofibre of the map from the constant diagram at F(∞); it is left adjoint to the inclusion and does not change gr^i since gr^i of a constant diagram vanishes.
Conservativity: if all gr^i F vanish, all transition maps are equivalences, so F is constant with value F(∞).

Day convolution along addition on ℤ^op gives the tensor product (HA Example 2.2.6.13 and Proposition 2.2.6.16); the gr formula follows by computing on the generators that are constant above an index; completion inverts the maps that are equivalences on gr, so the monoidal structure descends.
acceptance: For the filtration constant at X in degrees ≤ 0 and zero above, gr^0 = X and all other gr^i vanish.

For a module M over a ring A with ideal I, the I-adic filtration (I^i M for i ≥ 0, M for i ≤ 0) has completion whose underlying object is lim_i M/I^i M, the classical I-adic completion, although lim_i I^i M may have a nonzero lim¹ term (for ℤ and I = (p) it is ℤ_p/ℤ in degree 1).
A constant filtration with nonzero value has all gr^i zero but is nonzero: gr alone is not conservative on DF(C).

nodes.title: Perfect, compact and dualizable modules
nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring. For M ∈ D∞(R) the following are equivalent: (1) M is perfect, quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective R-modules; (2) M is a compact object of D∞(R); (3) M is dualizable in the symmetric monoidal ∞-category D∞(R). D∞(R) is compactly generated by R[0], the perfect complexes form a small idempotent-complete stable subcategory Perf(R) with Ind(Perf(R)) ≃ D∞(R), and extension of scalars along R → S preserves perfect complexes and duals. For a filtered colimit of rings R = colim_i R_i, Perf(R) ≃ colim_i Perf(R_i): every perfect R-complex is extended from some R_i, and mapping spaces between extended complexes are filtered colimits of mapping spaces over the R_j.
hypotheses: R is a discrete commutative ring; D∞(R) has the symmetric monoidal structure of E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-derived-sheaves.
Filtered colimits of rings are in commutative rings; the colimit of categories is in Cat∞.
The ordinary predicate 'perfect' is the one DerivedModuleAlgebra §1.E.0 (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) defines; this node states the enhanced comparison.
proofSteps: (1) ⇔ (2): bounded complexes of finite projectives are compact by a direct Hom computation, and a compact object is a retract of a bounded complex of finite projectives (Stacks Proposition 15.80.3).
(2) ⇔ (3): transport along Mod_{HR}(Sp) ≃ D∞(R) (E5:spectra-comparison/late-realisation) and use HA Proposition 7.2.4.4: a module is compact exactly when it admits a dual corepresenting Map(M, −).
Compact generation by R[0] and Ind(Perf(R)) ≃ D∞(R): HA Proposition 7.2.4.2 with E5:presentability/ind-completion.

Filtered colimits: on homotopy categories this is Stacks Lemma 15.76.18; coherently, module categories form a functor from rings to PrL preserving filtered colimits, and compact objects of a filtered colimit along compact-preserving functors are the colimit of compact objects (HA Lemmas 7.3.5.11–7.3.5.12).
acceptance: R[0] and R^n[k] are perfect, compact and dualizable, with dual Hom(R^n, R)[−k].
⊕_{n ∈ ℕ} ℤ[0] is neither perfect nor compact in D∞(ℤ): its identity does not factor through a finite subsum.
For R = colim_n ℤ[x^{1/p^n}] every perfect complex over R comes from some ℤ[x^{1/p^n}].

sources.match: In D(R), perfect and compact objects coincide; perfect complexes over a filtered colimit of rings are extended from a finite stage, with Hom groups the colimit.

Module categories over ring spectra are compactly generated, compact modules are the perfect ones and are characterized by having duals; the module functor preserves weakly contractible colimits and compact objects pass to filtered colimits of compactly generated categories.

nodes.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and θ : AnimAlg_R → CAlg(D(R)^{cn}) the sifted-colimit-preserving comparison of E5:cotangent-export/e-infinity-comparison-in-proved-ranges, where D(R)^{cn} is the connective part (cohomology in degrees ≤ 0). For B ∈ AnimAlg_R put Mod_B := Mod_{θB}(D(R)), modules in the sense of E5:abstract/module-objects, with relative tensor product ⊗^L_B. Then Mod_B is a presentably symmetric monoidal stable ∞-category with unit B; its connective part is generated under colimits by B; a map A → B gives extension of scalars − ⊗^L_A B : Mod_A → Mod_B, symmetric monoidal and left adjoint to restriction, transitive along A → B → C; and for discrete B there is a symmetric monoidal equivalence Mod_B ≃ D∞(B) carrying B to B[0], compatible with Mathlib's DerivedCategory (ModuleCat B) on homotopy categories.
hypotheses: R commutative; B animated over R; connective means cohomology in degrees ≤ 0.
θ is the comparison of the corrected E5:cotangent-export/e-infinity-comparison-in-proved-ranges; it need not be an equivalence, but Mod_B depends only on θB.
proofSteps: Apply the module construction of E5:abstract/module-objects to the commutative algebra θB of the presentably symmetric monoidal D(R) (E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-derived-sheaves); relative tensor products by the bar construction.
The connective part is generated by B under colimits (HA Proposition 7.1.1.13(1), transported along the module comparison).
Extension of scalars is the free-module functor; transitivity by uniqueness of adjoints.
For discrete B, Mod_{B[0]}(D(R)) ≃ Mod_{HB}(Sp) ≃ D∞(B) by E5:spectra-comparison/late-realisation applied to R and to B (HA Theorem 7.1.2.13 and Remark 7.1.1.16).
acceptance: Mod_R = D∞(R).
For discrete B, the unit of Mod_B corresponds to B[0] in D∞(B).
For B = 𝔽_p ⊗^L_ℤ 𝔽_p, π_1 B = 𝔽_p, so the unit of Mod_B is not discrete and Mod_B is not D∞(π_0 B).

nodes.title: Square-zero extensions and derived derivations
nodes.statement: Let A → B be a map of animated commutative rings and M a connective B-module. The trivial square-zero extension B ⊕ M is the animated A-algebra over B obtained by animating, on pairs (P, F) of a polynomial A-algebra P and a finite free P-module F, the ordinary square-zero extension P ⊕ F (Mathlib's TrivSqZeroExt) with multiplication (p, f)(p', f') = (pp', pf' + p'f). The space of A-derivations of B into M is Der_A(B, M) := Map_{AnimAlg_A/B}(B, B ⊕ M), the space of sections of the projection B ⊕ M → B, based at the zero section; it keeps all higher homotopy. For discrete B and discrete M, π_0 Der_A(B, M) is the set of ordinary A-derivations B → M. For ordinary B and M, B ⊕ M is the split trivial extension of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.5.
hypotheses: M is connective; the definition is stated in AnimAlg_A over B.
The square-zero multiplication is part of the definition; a product ring is not a square-zero extension.
proofSteps: Animate the functor (P, F) ↦ P ⊕ F on pairs, which preserves finite coproducts in the first variable, by E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation.
Define Der_A(B, M) as the fibre over id_B of the map of mapping spaces induced by the projection.
For discrete inputs, π_0 is computed by maps of ordinary algebras over B, which are derivations by Mathlib's derivationToSquareZeroEquivLift.
acceptance: Der_A(A, M) is contractible.
For B = A[t], Der_A(B, M) is the underlying space Ω^∞M of M, through δ ↦ δ(t).
For discrete M, a section sends t² to (t², 2tδ(t)).

nodes.title: The cotangent complex of animated rings
nodes.statement: For a map A → B of animated commutative rings, the cotangent complex L_{B/A} ∈ Mod_B is the connective B-module obtained by animating P ↦ Ω_{P/A} ⊗_P B on polynomial A-algebras P (with Ω the Kähler differentials), together with its scalar extension in both variables; a commutative square of animated rings (A → B) → (A' → B') induces L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B' → L_{B'/A'}, coherently in composites. All negative cohomology is retained. For ordinary rings A → B, L_{B/A} corresponds under the equivalence of the homotopy category of Mod_B with D(B) to the ordinary cotangent complex of DerivedModuleAlgebra (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) §0.4 (Algebra.CotangentComplex A B, the standard simplicial resolution model), compatibly with that roadmap's maps of squares and resolution comparisons (cotangentComplex_ordinary). Along this comparison the ordinary statements of that roadmap transport to L_{B/A}: H^0 L_{B/A} = Ω_{B/A} and the naive two-term truncation with H^{−1} = Algebra.H1Cotangent (§0.7), the smooth and étale computations (§0.12) and the regular-quotient formula L_{(P/J)/P} ≃ (J/J²)[1] (§0.13). The ordinary constructions and their proofs belong to that roadmap; PerfectoidSpaces Layer 0 (§0.19 of its package) consumes the same ordinary complex.
hypotheses: A → B is a map of animated commutative rings; the comparison statements are for ordinary A and B.
Cohomological indexing: connective means cohomology in degrees ≤ 0.
proofSteps: The functor P ↦ (P, Ω_{P/A}) from polynomial A-algebras to module pairs preserves finite coproducts; its animation (E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation) defines (B, L_{B/A}).

For ordinary A → B, a free simplicial polynomial resolution P_• → B computes the animation by geometric realization; its normalized complex is the model Algebra.CotangentComplex A B of DerivedModuleAlgebra (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) §0.4 (Stacks Lemmas 4.3 and Remark 5.5), which gives cotangentComplex_ordinary, natural in squares.

Transport DerivedModuleAlgebra (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) §§0.7, 0.12 and 0.13 along cotangentComplex_ordinary: the naive truncation is Mathlib's Algebra.Extension.cotangentComplex with its exactness lemma at Ω and Algebra.Generators.equivH1Cotangent, and regular sequences are Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular; naturality in squares by functoriality of the animation.
acceptance: L_{A[t]/A} ≃ A[t]·dt in degree 0.
For a field k of characteristic ≠ 2 and B = k[ε]/(ε²), L_{B/k} is [B → B dε] in degrees −1, 0 with 1 ↦ 2ε dε, so H^{−1} L_{B/k} = εB ≠ 0.
For k → k[ε]/(ε²) → k (ε ↦ 0), H^{−1} L_{k/k[ε]/(ε²)} = k and H^{−2} L_{k/k[ε]/(ε²)} = k: the naive truncation sees only H^{−1}.
L_{𝔽_p/ℤ} ≃ 𝔽_p[1], and for ℤ → ℤ[x, y]/(y − x²) the cotangent complex is free of rank 1 in degree 0.

nodes.title: The universal property of the cotangent complex
nodes.statement: For a map A → B of animated rings and a connective B-module M there is a natural equivalence Map_{Mod_B}(L_{B/A}, M) ≃ Der_A(B, M), compatible with module maps M → N and with commutative squares of animated rings. For ordinary A → B and an ordinary B-module M its π_0 is Ext^0_B(L_{B/A}, M) = Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) = Der_A(B, M), the Ext-zero correspondence of DerivedModuleAlgebra (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #944) §0.6 transported along cotangentComplex_ordinary; the Ext¹/Exal correspondence and the obstruction theory of square-zero lifts (§§0.6, 0.25 there) are not restated here.
hypotheses: M is connective.
proofSteps: For polynomial A-algebras both sides are the space of coordinate derivations; π_0 is Mathlib's derivation–lift correspondence derivationToSquareZeroEquivLift.
Both sides send sifted colimits of polynomial algebras (in B) to limits of spaces, so the equivalence extends uniquely by animation.
acceptance: For B = A[t] the equivalence is evaluation at dt.
For B = A both sides are contractible.
For ordinary A → B and M, π_0 recovers Hom_B(Ω_{B/A}, M) = Der_A(B, M).
For B = A[t] and M = B[1], the derivation space has π_1 = B: the set of ordinary derivations cannot supply the mapping-space equivalence.

For ordinary rings it corresponds under cotangentComplex_ordinary to the transitivity triangle of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.8.
hypotheses: Tensor products are derived; the sequence is a cofibre sequence in the stable ∞-category Mod_C.
proofSteps: For B polynomial over A and C polynomial over B, the sequence of modules of differentials is split exact.

Resolve the composable pair by a bisimplicial pair of polynomial algebras and realize; identify the three terms by the universal property (E5:cotangent-export/cotangent-universal-property) and extension of scalars.
For ordinary rings, compare with the triangle of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.8 (Stacks Proposition 7.4) through cotangentComplex_ordinary; both are determined on polynomial pairs.

nodes.title: Base change of the cotangent complex
nodes.statement: For an animated pushout B' = B ⊗^L_A A', the natural map L_{B/A} ⊗^L_B B' → L_{B'/A'} is an equivalence. For ordinary rings the formula holds for the ordinary pushout B ⊗_A A' exactly in the Tor-independent case Tor_i^A(B, A') = 0 for i > 0, where it corresponds under cotangentComplex_ordinary to DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.10.
hypotheses: The pushout is the animated (derived) one.
proofSteps: Base change a polynomial resolution of B along A → A'; the differentials of polynomial algebras base change; realize.
Under Tor-independence the animated pushout is discrete and equals the ordinary one (Stacks Lemma 6.2).
acceptance: Flat A → A': the ordinary pushout suffices.

For ℤ → 𝔽_p base changed along ℤ → 𝔽_p, the animated pushout B' = 𝔽_p ⊗^L_ℤ 𝔽_p has L_{B'/𝔽_p} ≃ B'[1] ≠ 0, while for the ordinary pushout 𝔽_p the formula would predict 𝔽_p[1] although L_{𝔽_p/𝔽_p} = 0.
For A' = A the map is the identity.

sources.match: If B ⊗^L_A A' is the ordinary pushout B', the cotangent complex of A' → B' is the base change of that of A → B.

nodes.title: Localization, étale maps and filtered colimits
nodes.statement: L_{B/A} vanishes when A → B is a localization S^{-1}A, an étale map, more generally weakly étale (A → B and B ⊗_A B → B flat), a flat epimorphism, or a filtered colimit of maps with vanishing cotangent complex. For multiplicative sets S ⊆ A and T ⊆ B with S mapping into T, L_{T^{-1}B/S^{-1}A} ≃ L_{B/A} ⊗_B T^{-1}B. For a filtered colimit B = colim_j B_j of animated A-algebras, L_{B/A} ≃ colim_j (L_{B_j/A} ⊗^L_{B_j} B). The localization and filtered-colimit formulas for ordinary rings correspond under cotangentComplex_ordinary to DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.11; the weakly étale and flat-epimorphism vanishing is stated here.

nodes.title: Derived exterior powers
nodes.statement: For an animated ring B and a connective B-module M, the derived exterior powers L∧^n_B(M), n ≥ 0, are the animation of the exterior power ∧^n on pairs (P, F) of a polynomial algebra and a finite free module (with ∧^n the quotient of the tensor power by the tensors with two equal factors). They are connective B-modules with base change L∧^n_B(M) ⊗^L_B B' ≃ L∧^n_{B'}(M ⊗^L_B B') and a graded multiplication; for discrete B and a flat discrete B-module M they are the ordinary exterior powers (Mathlib's exteriorPower). For discrete B the homotopy-category shadow of L∧^n_B is the derived exterior power DerivedDeRham.derivedExteriorPower of DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.14, which this node refines. Applied to M = L_{B/A} they give LΩ^n_{B/A} = L∧^n_B(L_{B/A}), which is Ω^n_{B/A}[0] when L_{B/A} is flat in degree 0 (for example B smooth over A).
hypotheses: M connective; exterior powers impose x ∧ x = 0 also in characteristic 2.
proofSteps: The exterior power on finite free modules over polynomial algebras preserves the relevant finite coproducts in the ring variable; animate it on module pairs (E5:animation/nonabelian-derived-category, E5:animation/universal-property-of-animation; SAG Construction 25.2.2.2).

Base change: both sides commute with sifted colimits, so it suffices to treat finite free modules extended from ℤ, where it is the explicit description of ∧^n on free modules (SAG Proposition 25.2.3.1); the multiplication by animation of the ordinary one.

The flat comparison: both sides commute with filtered colimits in M, so Lazard's theorem reduces it to finite free M (SAG Proposition 25.2.3.4, with the exterior power in place of the signed-coinvariant quotient printed there, see sourceIssues).
For M = L_{B/A} this is BL22 Construction B.1; the smooth case is BL22 Remark B.5. For discrete B, compare with DerivedModuleAlgebra §0.14 on finite free modules.
acceptance: L∧^0_B(M) = B and L∧^1_B(M) = M.
For the free rank-one module Be, L∧^2(Be) = 0, also over 𝔽_2.
For B smooth over A, L∧^n(L_{B/A}) = Ω^n_{B/A}[0].

sources.locator: Construction B.1, p. 225; Remark B.5, p. 226
sources.match: Bhatt and Lurie define the derived exterior powers of the cotangent complex for animated algebras as the sifted-colimit extension of the exterior powers of differentials, and note that they are the ordinary differential forms when the cotangent complex is flat in degree 0.

fields.statement: For a cosimplicial diagram of n-truncated spaces, n≥0 fixed, totalization equals partial totalization through degree n+1. Consequently totalization commutes with filtered colimits when the truncation bound is uniform in both indices. For cosimplicial spectra whose terms all lie in Sp≤b for one integer b, π_k of totalization is computed by a finite partial stage r≥max(0,b−k+1). This gives filtered-colimit commutation degree by degree; coconnective terms are the case b=0. The analogous cohomological comparison for complexes uses a uniform lower cohomological bound. Without a uniform bound, arbitrary totalization need not commute with filtered colimits. Unbounded Postnikov convergence and hypercompleteness are not used.
